title: Tswana peoples across the territory
description: After generations of migration the Tswana-speaking peoples have a presence throughout what is now Botswana, organised in chiefdoms ruled by dikgosi.

title: Kololo expelled
description: In the turmoil of the Difaqane the Kololo attack the north-western Tswana, and the Kwena and Ngwaketse surround them and drive them from the region.

title: Livingstone arrives
description: The Scottish missionary David Livingstone arrives and sets up a mission at Kolobeng, the start of heavier European involvement in the Tswana chiefdoms.

title: Chief Sechele baptised
description: Sechele of the Kwena is the first person Livingstone converts to Christianity, and the chief spreads the new faith among the Tswana.

title: Battle of Dimawe
description: A Transvaal Boer commando fights a coalition of Tswana chiefdoms, and the war ends Boer expansion westward into what is now Botswana.

title: Tati gold rush
description: The discovery of gold on the Tati river starts the first European gold rush of southern Africa.

title: Bechuanaland Protectorate proclaimed
description: At the request of Tswana chiefs threatened by the Boers and the Germans, Britain proclaims a protectorate over Bechuanaland.

title: Three chiefs travel to London
description: Khama III, Bathoen I and Sebele I campaign in Britain against handing their land to Cecil Rhodes's company, and the protectorate is kept under the Crown.

title: Seretse Khama marries Ruth Williams
description: The heir to the Ngwato chieftaincy marries an English clerk, a union to which South Africa objects and which sets off a political crisis.

title: Seretse exiled
description: The British government refuses to recognise Seretse Khama as chief of the Ngwato and banishes him and his wife from his own country.

title: Seretse returns
description: Seretse and Ruth Khama are allowed back to popular acclaim, and he soon turns to nationalist politics.

title: Democratic Party founded
description: Seretse Khama founds the Bechuanaland Democratic Party, which will win every election for more than half a century.

title: First general election
description: Seretse Khama's Democratic Party wins the first election by universal adult suffrage, setting Botswana on its path as a stable democracy.

title: Capital moves to Gaborone
description: The seat of government leaves Mafeking, outside the territory, for the new purpose-built capital at Gaborone.

title: Independence
description: Botswana becomes independent as a republic with Seretse Khama as its first president, then one of the poorest countries in the world.

title: Diamonds found at Orapa
description: Prospectors locate one of the world's largest diamond pipes, the discovery on which Botswana's economic rise is built.

title: Defence Force formed
description: Under attack from Rhodesian and later South African cross-border operations, Botswana sets up its first standing army.

title: Seretse Khama dies
description: The founding president dies in office and Vice-President Quett Masire succeeds him.

title: South Africa raids Gaborone
description: South African forces cross the border and kill twelve people in an operation against exiled opponents of apartheid.

title: Festus Mogae becomes president
description: Quett Masire retires after eighteen years and hands the presidency to Festus Mogae in a routine transfer of power.

title: Ian Khama becomes president
description: Seretse Khama's son, the former army commander Ian Khama, takes over the presidency for a decade.

title: Masisi becomes president
description: Mokgweetsi Masisi succeeds Ian Khama, and the two soon fall out in a feud that splits the ruling party.

title: General election
description: The governing Democratic Party wins again in elections whose result the opposition challengers contest in court.
